final_report.summary: Successfully diagnosed and fixed the widget control dropdown z-index/stacking context bug in the AtlasForge dashboard. The widget control toolbar (lock/unlock + widget visibility dropdown) was rendering beneath the main tab navigation bar due to CSS stacking context hierarchy. The fix used the DOM Portal pattern — moving #widget-vis-dropdown and #preset-dropdown to be direct children of <body> at initialization, assigning z-index: 10000 and position: fixed, thereby escaping all ancestor stacking contexts. All 15 functional tests passed confirming the fix is complete and regression-free.
key_achievements: Identified root cause: CSS stacking context hierarchy where .main-tabs nav (z-index 99) painted over the header dropdown regardless of declared z-index on the dropdown elements

Diagnosed three contributing factors: DOM paint order, overflow-x: auto on .header-row-2 creating a clipping stacking context, and sticky nav creating its own stacking context outranking the dropdown's parent
Implemented DOM Portal pattern: moved #widget-vis-dropdown and #preset-dropdown to document.body at init time, escaping all ancestor stacking contexts
Applied position: fixed + z-index: 10000 to both portaled dropdowns ensuring they always render above all page layers

Verified fix with a 15-test Selenium/Firefox functional test suite covering portal attachment, z-index values, overflow clipping, open/close behavior, viewport visibility, positioning, and adversarial regressions
All 15/15 tests passed — no regressions on lock button or preset dropdown functionality
challenges_overcome: Stacking context complexity: multiple overlapping stacking contexts (overflow-x: auto container, sticky nav) combined to trap the dropdown regardless of z-index on the dropdown itself
Mobile vs desktop divergence: overflow-x: auto on the header row created a clipping context that would have prevented position: absolute solutions from escaping
Rejected simpler approaches (increasing header z-index, reordering HTML) as insufficient — only the portal pattern fully escapes all ancestor stacking contexts
Ensuring outside-click close behavior still worked correctly after moving dropdowns out of their original DOM parent context
lessons_learned: When a dropdown renders beneath a sibling element despite high z-index, the issue is almost always a stacking context on an ancestor — not the z-index value itself
overflow-x: auto/scroll on a container creates a stacking context, which is a common and easily missed culprit in header/nav layout bugs
The DOM Portal pattern (appending to document.body + position: fixed) is the definitive solution for any dropdown/modal that must escape ancestor stacking contexts
Functional Selenium tests are far more reliable than unit tests for verifying CSS stacking context fixes — CSS behavior cannot be reliably tested without a real rendering engine
Three-option analysis (increase z-index / reorder HTML / portal to body) before implementing avoids wasted effort on approaches that don't fully solve the problem
